sections.h2: Selling an Urbana house: your options
sections.html:
Listing through an agent, selling alone and accepting a cash buyer's as-is price all work in Urbana. Tenants change the picture, because the city runs a rental registration program, and the University of Illinois next door keeps the rental market busy.

Urbana sits in Champaign County, shares its western edge with the city of Champaign, and holds most of the university campus. Population was 38,336 at the 2020 count and is estimated at 39,719 for mid-2025.

This is a young, renter-heavy city where home values sit far under those in the Chicago suburbs. Only 37.3% of homes are lived in by their owners: there are 10,569 renter-occupied units against 6,287 owner-occupied ones, across 16,856 households.

The middle value of an owned home is $184,900, and the middle rent with utilities is $972 a month. Median household income is $45,346. Median age is 27.2, and 72.8% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. If you own a house here, your likely buyers are other owners, investors and families tied to the university.

The city has more than 10,000 rental units, nearly two-thirds of its housing, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign enrolls more than 50,000 students annually. The city runs a Rental Registration and Inspection Program, described on its program page.

  • Every rental property must register each year and pay a fee from the city's schedule of fees.
  • The program year runs from October 15 to October 14, matching the leasing calendar.
  • It covers single-family homes, duplexes and multi-family buildings, including room rentals where the owner also lives there.
  • Nursing homes, hotels and motels, housing authority units and university-certified housing are excluded.
  • The city aims to inspect every rental on a cycle of three to five years, and results appear in its open data portal.

Landlords register through an online Citizenserve account, and the Building Safety Division answers questions at 217-384-2443. If you own a rental, make sure the registration is current before you list, and ask the division what the inspection record shows.

sections.h2: Property tax bills and due dates
sections.html:
The Champaign County Treasurer and Collector bills and collects the tax from the Bennett Administrative Center at 102 E. Main Street in Urbana, phone 217-384-3743. The county mails one bill for the full year with coupons for two equal installments, and no second bill follows. The office handles more than 77,000 real estate bills for 156 taxing districts, including school districts, cities and villages.

Champaign County real estate tax calendar, repeating each year
Time of yearWhat happens
May 1Bills are mailed
Early JuneFirst installment due
Early SeptemberSecond installment due
September 30, 4:30 p.m.Last day to pay by check, e-check or card; later payments are cash, money order or cashier's check
October 1A $10 cost is added to each unpaid parcel for notices and publication
December 1 to 31Advance payments accepted, from 50% of the prior year's total up to 10% over it

Postmarks do not count for the late-payment dates, so pay early. If the county has an old mailing address for you, call the Supervisor of Assessments at 217-384-3760.

The Treasurer's tax page lists the programs and the office that handles each one. Most go through the County Assessment Office at 217-384-3760, which is also the number for corrections to bill information.

  • Owner-occupied exemption
  • Over-65 exemption for real estate, and the Senior Assessment Freeze
  • Disabled persons exemption and various exemptions for military service
  • Natural disaster homestead exemption
  • Tax deferral for owners over 65, run by the County Treasurer

Before you sell, ask the assessment office what is on file for the parcel, so the buyer's first bill is not a surprise.

Champaign County has elected to act as trustee for the taxing districts on delinquent real estate taxes, beginning with the 2025 taxes payable in 2026 (Public Act 104-0553). At the delinquent sale, the county takes the taxes in place of private tax buyers.

If back taxes are owed, get a payoff from the Treasurer before a closing date is fixed. The title company will find the balance anyway, and the amount comes out of your proceeds at the table. Knowing it early lets you judge any offer by what you would actually keep.

sections.h2: Inherited house and the seller disclosure
sections.html:
An inherited Urbana house may not need the usual seller disclosure. Illinois expects residential sellers to give the buyer a disclosure report ahead of signing (765 ILCS 77/20), but Section 15 exempts several kinds of seller, including a fiduciary administering a decedent's estate, a transfer from a decedent by will or intestate succession, and transfers made under court order.

Who signs the deed decides whether an exemption applies, so check with the closing attorney. The Champaign County Recorder can tell you the current deed requirements and fees before you schedule a signing.

Once an offer is accepted, the title company searches the records for the parcel and lists anything owed against it. You request payoff letters from any lender, collect your latest tax bill, and agree on a closing date with the buyer.

For a rental, bring the current registration and any inspection results, and give tenants proper notice under their lease. A buyer paying cash has no lender appraisal to wait on, so the timeline comes down to the title work and when the deed reaches the Champaign County Recorder. Bring photo ID to the signing, plus any keys, garage openers and warranty papers you have for the house.

faqs.q: Does the city of Urbana inspect a house before it sells?
faqs.a: The city's permit and rental pages describe permits and a rental inspection cycle. Call the Building Safety Division at 217-384-2443 to ask whether anything applies to a sale at your address.

faqs.q: What dates apply to Urbana property tax installments?
faqs.a: There are two installments, with bills going out May 1. The first is due in early June and the second in early September, and the pattern repeats yearly.

faqs.q: What should the owner of an Urbana rental do before listing?
faqs.a: Confirm that registration is current, because the program year runs October 15 to October 14 and fees are annual. The Building Safety Division can explain the inspection history, which also appears in the city's open data.

faqs.q: Where can an Urbana owner pay property tax in person?
faqs.a: Pay at the Champaign County Treasurer's Office, 102 E. Main Street in Urbana. A 24-hour drop box sits in front of the guard shack in the parking area, and cash, checks, money orders and cards are accepted, with cards and checks only through September 30.

faqs.q: How fast can a cash sale of an Urbana house close?
faqs.a: It moves as fast as the title work, payoff letters and deed are ready. A cash closing depends on the buyer's funds, the title company and the county's recording of the deed.
